fields.description:
Discovered by the Step-7 sibling sweep while fixing bug 747f (blobless snapshot materialization).

747f added `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300` to `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py`, joining the existing precedent in `src/rebar/_store/push.py:57` and `src/rebar/_store/sync.py:58` (`_GIT_TIMEOUT = 30`). The sweep found the *timeout* half of that bug class still live at other network-capable git call sites, each of which can block indefinitely on a stuck remote or a hung credential helper. 747f proved this is not theoretical: an unbounded git call on the materialize path produced 40 sequential per-object fetch RPCs and a measured ~2.1-hour hang.

## Scope — deliberately narrowed by the operator; recorded here, not silently

The original sweep listed 8 call sites. This ticket now covers SIX of them, in three modules. The other two were SPLIT OUT, not dropped:

**Deferred to task 983f-ee85-1e06-428e (rainbow-interested-kusimanse), linked `discovered_from` this ticket:**
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — `fetch <remote> <branch>`
- `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` — `push origin HEAD:tickets`

**Reason for the split:** bug 01e8-302b-ab8f-4220 is IN PROGRESS in another session covering store/init/sync divergence and has already modified `init.py` and the fsck path. 01e8 declares no `file_impact`, so the overlap cannot be verified precisely, and the operator chose not to guess rather than risk a conflicting edit. 983f carries a `depends_on` link to 01e8 and is blocked until it closes.

## The six in-scope sites, re-verified against origin/main @ ed9d5e28d

**A. `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` (2 sites) — ALREADY BOUNDED; the original sweep note is STALE.**

`_remote_ref_absent` -> `ls-remote --exit-code` and `_push_lease_cas` -> `push --force-with-lease` both already pass `timeout=_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS` (30.0s). This is structurally guaranteed, not incidental: the module's single git seam `_git(repo_root, args, *, timeout: float, ...)` declares `timeout` as a REQUIRED keyword-only parameter with no default, and it holds the module's only `run_git` call, so an unbounded git call is unrepresentable there. A timeout already surfaces as `RefLockTimeoutError` naming the operation and the bound, fail-closed (treated as HELD). **No edit is required or made here** — which also honours the standing instruction not to touch `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/**` while a parallel session owns it.

**B. `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py::clone_change_ref` — UNBOUNDED, fixed by this ticket.**

Five `subprocess.run` calls, none passing a timeout: `git init`, `fetch --depth 2 <repo_url> <revision_ref>`, `checkout FETCH_HEAD`, `remote add origin`, `fetch --depth 1 origin refs/heads/tickets`. The two fetches are network-capable. Additionally `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` is neither an `OSError` nor a `CalledProcessError`, so it sits outside the existing `except` tuple — a timeout would escape the token-redacting handler entirely, and `TimeoutExpired.cmd` carries the `user:token@host` fetch URL, making an unredacted timeout a credential-leak path as well as a hang.

**C. `src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py` — UNBOUNDED, fixed by this ticket.**

The single `_git(cwd, *args)` helper calls `subprocess.run(...)` with no timeout, so EVERY git call in the module is unbounded, including the two network-capable ones: `fetch --quiet review <branch>` and `fetch --quiet tickets <branch>`. A `TimeoutExpired` would also bypass `_git_ok`'s `WorkspaceError` conversion.

## Value chosen: `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300`, matching 747f rather than `_store`

Both live modules do a COLD fetch into a freshly created directory (`gerrit_client` runs `git init` on a new dest per change; `workspace` fetches into a fresh `mkdtemp`), and `workspace`'s fetches are not even shallow. That is 747f's profile — a legitimately large RPC, legitimately minutes on a cold clone — not the `_store` profile, which is an INCREMENTAL ref-sized push/fetch against an already-warm clone and so is correctly bound at 30s. Choosing 30s here would risk breaking a working cold-clone path; 300s converts an unbounded hang into a bounded, diagnosable failure without narrowing any legitimate one. One constant per module (not a per-call-site matrix) matches the existing `_GIT_TIMEOUT` precedent instead of inventing a new mechanism.

## Resolved: the `git archive` question (was flagged UNJUDGED)

`src/rebar/llm/workflow/snapshot.py` materializes via `git archive --format=tar <sha>`, and the sweep asked whether it degrades like the `read-tree`/`checkout-index` pair 747f fixed. **Measured read-only; answer NO.** On a 40-file `--filter=blob:none` fixture with `uploadpack.allowFilter` enabled (git 2.55.0), `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` `child_start` counting shows 40 missing blobs resolved by exactly ONE batched child `git fetch ... --filter=blob:none --stdin`, versus 40 separate sequential fetches for the primitive pair 747f fixed. `git archive` therefore DOES batch its promisor prefetch and is NOT an instance of the 747f bug class. No change made and no follow-up filed; the file is owned by a parallel session and was inspected read-only only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py` defines a module-level `_GIT_TIMEOUT` and all five `clone_change_ref` subprocess calls pass it, with a comment justifying 300 against the cited 747f and `_store` precedents.
- [ ] `src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py` defines a module-level `_GIT_TIMEOUT` and its single `_git` helper passes it, so every git call in the module is bounded.
- [ ] A `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` in `clone_change_ref` is converted to a `GerritError` that names the timed-out git operation and the bound, and is routed through the EXISTING token-redaction path so the `user:token@host` URL never appears in the message.
- [ ] A `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` in `workspace._git` is converted to a `WorkspaceError` that names the timed-out git operation and the bound, never propagating the raw exception.
- [ ] The two `_ref_lock.py` sites are confirmed already bounded and left unedited, with that confirmation recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] The two deferred `_commands/` sites are recorded on task 983f-ee85-1e06-428e with their blocking reason, NOT silently dropped from scope.
- [ ] Verified by the commands in the Testing section below: the new held-out test passes, and lint, typecheck, and the default suite all exit zero.

## Testing

A new held-out test file `tests/unit/test_git_timeout_bounds_77e1.py` is written BEFORE the fix and proven RED first, then run GREEN against the implementation, and mutation-checked by reverting the timeout to confirm it returns to RED. It asserts, without any network access (the git call is monkeypatched to raise `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`):

1. Both modules expose a positive numeric `_GIT_TIMEOUT`, mirroring the `tests/unit/test_snapshot_blobless_747f.py` assertion shape.
2. Every `clone_change_ref` subprocess invocation receives a `timeout` kwarg.
3. A timing-out `clone_change_ref` raises `GerritError` (not `TimeoutExpired`), the message names the git operation and the bound, and the bot token does NOT appear in it.
4. A timing-out `workspace._git` raises `WorkspaceError` (not `TimeoutExpired`) naming the operation and the bound.

Proving commands, all run from the worktree with its venv first on `PATH`:

- `pytest tests/unit/test_git_timeout_bounds_77e1.py -q`
- `pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot.py tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py -q` (no regression in the two modules' existing coverage)
- `make lint`
- `make typecheck`
- `make test`
